PROP
39
PROHIBITS CITIZENS FROM VOTING UNLESS THEY PRESENT GOVERNMENT-ISSUED IDENTIFICATION. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Invalidates mail ballots that do not have last four digits of designated government-issued identification number written on envelope. Prohibits in-person voting without presenting government-issued identification. Fiscal Impact: Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements. Supporters: The Transparency Foundation; Latino American Political Assn; Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Assn; CA Women’s Leadership Assn Opponents: ACLU California Action; Common Cause; League of Women Voters of California
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: A voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Yes on Prop. 39 gives California a BIPARTISAN solution for VOTER ID. Supported by a solid majority of Democratic, Independent and Republican voters. Increases trust and confidence in our elections.
CON
No on Prop. 39. This would advance Trump’s voter suppression agenda by adding costly, unnecessary barriers that could block eligible California voters, expose personal information to identity theft, and waste hundreds of millions in taxpayer dollars. Don’t let MAGA billionaires decide which voters count. Vote No.

### PROPOSAL
Eliminates Ability of Multistate Businesses to Choose How Taxable Income Is Determined.
Under this measure, starting in 2013, multistate businesses would no longer be allowed to choose the method for determining their state taxable income that is most advantageous for them.
Instead, most multistate businesses would have to determine their California taxable income using the single sales factor method.
Businesses that operate only in California would be unaffected by this measure.
This measure also includes rules regarding how all multistate businesses calculate the portion of some sales that are allocated to California for state tax purposes.
These include a set of specific rules for certain large cable companies.

- Dedicates $550 million annually for five years from anticipated increase in revenue for the
purpose of funding projects that create energy efficiency and clean energy jobs in California.

## California Secretary of State Shirley N. Weber, Ph.D., Announces the Statewide Voter Information Guide for the November 3, 2026, General Election Is Available for Public Review
**Sacramento, Calif.** – Today California Secretary of State Shirley N. Weber, Ph.D., made the November 3, 2026, California General Election Official Voter Information Guide available for public review.
The guide, which will be mailed to every voting household in California, includes information about propositions and statements from candidates running for constitutional offices, as well as other important election information such as the California Voter Bill of Rights and information about how eligible Californians can vote.
California’s Official Voter Information Guide is available in 10 languages—English, Spanish, Chinese, Hindi, Japanese, Khmer, Korean, Tagalog, Thai, and Vietnamese.
The guide is available for public examination from July 21, 2026 through August 10, 2026 at https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/public-display and at the Office of the Secretary of State’s Sacramento and Los Angeles locations.

Following the conclusion of the public examination period, the Office of the Secretary of State will begin printing and mailing the statewide Voter Information Guide to all households that have at least one registered voter.

PROP
39
PROHIBITS CITIZENS FROM VOTING UNLESS THEY PRESENT GOVERNMENT-ISSUED IDENTIFICATION. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Invalidates mail ballots that do not have last four digits of designated government-issued identification number written on envelope. Prohibits in-person voting without presenting government-issued identification. Fiscal Impact: Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements. Supporters: The Transparency Foundation; Latino American Political Assn; Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Assn; CA Women’s Leadership Assn Opponents: ACLU California Action; Common Cause; League of Women Voters of California
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: A voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Yes on Prop. 39 gives California a BIPARTISAN solution for VOTER ID. Supported by a solid majority of Democratic, Independent and Republican voters. Increases trust and confidence in our elections.
CON
No on Prop. 39. This would advance Trump’s voter suppression agenda by adding costly, unnecessary barriers that could block eligible California voters, expose personal information to identity theft, and waste hundreds of millions in taxpayer dollars. Don’t let MAGA billionaires decide which voters count. Vote No.

**Sacramento, Calif.** – Today California Secretary of State Shirley N. Weber, Ph.D., made the November 3, 2026, California General Election Official Voter Information Guide available for public review.
The guide, which will be mailed to every voting household in California, includes information about propositions and statements from candidates running for constitutional offices, as well as other important election information such as the California Voter Bill of Rights and information about how eligible Californians can vote.
California’s Official Voter Information Guide is available in 10 languages—English, Spanish, Chinese, Hindi, Japanese, Khmer, Korean, Tagalog, Thai, and Vietnamese.

PROP
39
PROHIBITS CITIZENS FROM VOTING UNLESS THEY PRESENT GOVERNMENT-ISSUED IDENTIFICATION. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Invalidates mail ballots that do not have last four digits of designated government-issued identification number written on envelope. Prohibits in-person voting without presenting government-issued identification. Fiscal Impact: Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements. Supporters: The Transparency Foundation; Latino American Political Assn; Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Assn; CA Women’s Leadership Assn Opponents: ACLU California Action; Common Cause; League of Women Voters of California
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: A voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Yes on Prop. 39 gives California a BIPARTISAN solution for VOTER ID. Supported by a solid majority of Democratic, Independent and Republican voters. Increases trust and confidence in our elections.
CON
No on Prop. 39. This would advance Trump’s voter suppression agenda by adding costly, unnecessary barriers that could block eligible California voters, expose personal information to identity theft, and waste hundreds of millions in taxpayer dollars. Don’t let MAGA billionaires decide which voters count. Vote No.
FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

Eliminates Ability of Multistate Businesses to Choose How Taxable Income Is Determined.
Under this measure, starting in 2013, multistate businesses would no longer be allowed to choose the method for determining their state taxable income that is most advantageous for them.

# California voter ID measure falling short in new poll
By Lindsey Holden
10/19/2026 8:21 PM UTC
SACRAMENTO, California — California’s voter ID measure is falling short of majority support, with likely voters deeply divided along party lines, according to a new Citrin-POLITICO poll.
Fifty-one percent of likely voters polled said they would vote against Proposition 39, which would require Californians to show ID at polling places and add the last few digits of an ID number to mail-in ballots.
Forty-two percent said they would vote in favor of it, while 7% remained undecided.
Those results are in line with September polls from the Berkeley Institute for Governmental Studies and the Public Policy Institute of California, both of which had the measure losing by similar margins.
...
Eighty percent of Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents said they would vote ‘no,’ while 92% of Republicans and Republican-leaning independents said they’re prepared to vote ‘yes.’
Independents favor the measure by a small margin, 45% to 41%.

5. Party ID: Democrats outnumber Republicans roughly 2:1 in California. 80% of Democrats/Dem-leaning say No, 92% of Republicans say Yes. Independents split. That math in a Democratic-leaning electorate favors No.

- Mason-Dixon (Sept 21-24): Yes +7
- SurveyUSA (Sept 15-20): Yes +10
- Berkeley IGS (Sept 15-20): No +13
- PPIC (Sept 4-10): No +12

The trend over time: early in the year (April Berkeley IGS), it was leading 56-39. As the campaign progressed and the No side ramped up spending, it has fallen behind. Most recent, high-quality polls (Berkeley IGS, PPIC) show the No side leading by 17-20 points.

Fundraising: Yes: ~$36.5 million (mostly from out-of-state billionaires Richard Uihlein $17M, Joe Gebbia $8M). No: ~$33.5 million (California Democratic Party, labor unions, etc.). Roughly comparable in the end.

Key factors:
1. California is a deep blue state; Democrats heavily oppose.
2. The No side has unified Democratic establishment support: Governor Newsom, gubernatorial frontrunner Xavier Becerra, Democratic Party, labor unions.
3. Polling trend has moved against the measure - support has dwindled as the election neared.
4. Historical pattern: voter ID type measures in California tend to fail. Also ballot measures in California often lose support as election day approaches (initiatives start high and decline).
5. Party ID: Democrats outnumber Republicans roughly 2:1 in California. 80% of Democrats/Dem-leaning say No, 92% of Republicans say Yes. Independents split. That math in a Democratic-leaning electorate favors No.

The most recent polls (late October 2026) show No leading by 20 points (Berkeley IGS) and 17 points (PPIC). Two Republican-leaning pollsters show it close (McLaughlin No+2, M3 No+6). SurveyUSA shows Yes+7 (an outlier).

Based on my extensive research on California Proposition 39 (the November 2026 voter ID initiative):

**Key evidence:**
- **Most recent polling consistently shows the measure losing**: Berkeley IGS (Oct 19–25) has No leading 57%–37%; PPIC (Oct 16–22) has No up 58%–41%; Citrin/Politico has No up 51%–42%. Even Republican-leaning pollsters (M3 Strategies, McLaughlin) show it trailing slightly.
- **Clear downward trend**: The measure led 56%–39% in April, but support steadily eroded as the opposition campaign ramped up — a classic pattern for California ballot initiatives.
- **Hostile political environment**: California's electorate is heavily Democratic (80% of Democrats/Dem-leaners oppose), and opponents successfully tied the measure to Trump, whose administration is actively litigating against California's election practices. The unified opposition includes Gov. Newsom, gubernatorial frontrunner Xavier Becerra (leading his race by ~16 points), the state Democratic Party, labor unions, ACLU, Common Cause, and the League of Women Voters.
- **Fundraising is roughly at parity** (Yes: ~$36.5M, mostly from out-of-state billionaires; No: ~$33.5M from the Democratic Party, unions, and tribes), so the Yes side's early money advantage no longer insulates it.

No

39
PROHIBITS CITIZENS FROM VOTING UNLESS THEY PRESENT GOVERNMENT-ISSUED IDENTIFICATION. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Invalidates mail ballots that do not have last four digits of designated government-issued identification number written on envelope. Prohibits in-person voting without presenting government-issued identification. Fiscal Impact: Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements. Supporters: The Transparency Foundation; Latino American Political Assn; Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Assn; CA Women’s Leadership Assn Opponents: ACLU California Action; Common Cause; League of Women Voters of California
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: A voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Yes on Prop. 39 gives California a BIPARTISAN solution for VOTER ID. Supported by a solid majority of Democratic, Independent and Republican voters. Increases trust and confidence in our elections.
CON
No on Prop. 39. This would advance Trump’s voter suppression agenda by adding costly, unnecessary barriers that could block eligible California voters, expose personal information to identity theft, and waste hundreds of millions in taxpayer dollars. Don’t let MAGA billionaires decide which voters count. Vote No.

Based on my extensive research on California Proposition 39 (the November 2026 voter ID initiative):

**Key evidence:**
- **Most recent polling consistently shows the measure losing**: Berkeley IGS (Oct 19–25) has No leading 57%–37%; PPIC (Oct 16–22) has No up 58%–41%; Citrin/Politico has No up 51%–42%. Even Republican-leaning pollsters (M3 Strategies, McLaughlin) show it trailing slightly.
- **Clear downward trend**: The measure led 56%–39% in April, but support steadily eroded as the opposition campaign ramped up — a classic pattern for California ballot initiatives.
- **Hostile political environment**: California's electorate is heavily Democratic (80% of Democrats/Dem-leaners oppose), and opponents successfully tied the measure to Trump, whose administration is actively litigating against California's election practices. The unified opposition includes Gov. Newsom, gubernatorial frontrunner Xavier Becerra (leading his race by ~16 points), the state Democratic Party, labor unions, ACLU, Common Cause, and the League of Women Voters.
- **Fundraising is roughly at parity** (Yes: ~$36.5M, mostly from out-of-state billionaires; No: ~$33.5M from the Democratic Party, unions, and tribes), so the Yes side's early money advantage no longer insulates it.
